extracted.intended_audience: patent owners, in-house counsel, and litigators evaluating U.S. post‑grant challenge forum options
extracted.subtask_description: Comparative summary of U.S. post‑grant patent proceedings (IPR, PGR, ex parte reexamination, reissue, supplemental examination) and related forums (district court, ITC) to guide selection and strategy. Lists procedural features, standards, timing, costs, decision makers, and practical benefits/limits for each forum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and Benefits of the Proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: High‑level description of what each proceeding is intended to accomplish and its practical advantages/limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPR: "Canceling one or more claims in less time, and at a lower cost, than district court, with minimal discovery."; PGR: "Canceling or compelling narrowing amendment of one or more claims in relatively slow, low cost ex parte forum with no advocacy by requester after initial request, no discovery, low standard of review, and broad claim interpretation."; Ex Parte Reexamination (XPR): "Canceling or adding one or more claims by right (narrower at any time before patent expires, or broader if filed within two years of issuance) in relatively slow, low cost ex parte forum with no discovery, low standard of review, and broad claim interpretation."; Reissue: (similar to XPR—canceling or adding claims by right); Supplemental Examination: "Curing possible defects relating to inequitable conduct in relatively slow, low cost ex parte forum with no discovery, lower standard of review and broader claim interpretation."; District Courts: "Invalidating one or more claims; finding of unenforceability; finding of infringement or non‑infringement; obtaining injunction and damages for infringement."; ITC: "Invalidating one or more claims; finding of unenforceability; obtaining exclusion order."

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption of Validity
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the patent is presumed valid in the forum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPR/PGR/Ex Parte Reexamination/Reissue/Supplemental Examination: "No presumption of validity."; District Courts/ITC: "Yes" (i.e., patents are presumed valid in district court and ITC proceedings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standing (Who May Seek Review?)
rubrics_metrics.description: Who is eligible to file or request the proceeding in each forum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPR: "Third party (who is not the U.S.) who is not a plaintiff challenging validity of patent or had been served with a complaint alleging infringement more than one year before IPR filing."; PGR: "Third party (who is not the U.S.) who is not a plaintiff challenging validity of patent."; Ex Parte Reexamination: "Patent Owner, third party (can be anonymous) and USPTO director."; Reissue: "Patent Owner only."; Supplemental Examination: "Patent Owner only."; District Courts: "Patent Owner or exclusive licensee alleging an actual case for infringement; third party seeking a declaratory judgment of invalidity, unenforceability, or non‑infringement."; ITC: "Patent Owner or exclusive licensee are required to be a complainant alleging infringement (other parties may join complaint); must have domestic industry relating to the protected product."

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualification of Patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Which patents are eligible for the forum (timing or claim date limitations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPR/PGR/Ex Parte Reexamination/Reissue/Supplemental Examination/District Courts/ITC: "Any patent."; Note: IPR/PGR apply only to patents having at least one claim with an effective filing date on or after March 16, 2013 (AIA cut‑off).

rubrics_metrics.name: When the Challenge Can Be Filed
rubrics_metrics.description: Timing restrictions for filing a challenge in each forum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPR: "For pre‑AIA patents, any time; for AIA patents (having at least one claim with an effective filing date on or after March 16, 2013), on or after 9 months after issuance or reissuance, or termination of PGR."; PGR: "Within 9 months of issuance or reissuance for patents having at least one claim with an effective filing date on or after March 16, 2013."; Ex Parte Reexamination: "Any time during enforceability of the patent (up to 6 years after lapse or expiration)."; Reissue: "Any time before patent expires."; Supplemental Examination: "Anytime during enforceability of the patent (up to 6 years after lapse or expiration)."; District Courts: "Any time before six years after expiration of the patent or six years after last infringing conduct."; ITC: "Any time before patent expires."

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted Grounds of Challenge
rubrics_metrics.description: Statutory grounds (e.g., 35 U.S.C. sections) that can be raised in the forum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPR: "35 U.S.C. §§ 102 and 103 based on patents and printed publications."; PGR: "Any grounds (35 U.S.C. §§ 101, 102, 103, 112) except § 112 failure to comply with 'best mode' requirement."; Ex Parte Reexamination/Reissue/Supplemental Examination: "Any grounds (35 U.S.C. §§ 101, 102, 103, 112) except § 112 best mode (ex parte/reissue specifics vary)."; District Courts/ITC: Not limited to statutory sections in the same way — district courts handle invalidity defenses broadly; ITC handles unfair acts and importation complaints (requires pleading showing unfair competition/unfair act and domestic industry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior Art Considered
rubrics_metrics.description: Types of prior art that the forum will consider when adjudicating patentability/validity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPR/PGR: "Limited to patents and printed publications."; Ex Parte Reexamination/Reissue/Supplemental Examination/District Courts/ITC: "All statutory prior art (i.e., patents, printed publications, prior art products and prior art acts)."

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for Initiating Review
rubrics_metrics.description: Threshold standard the petitioner must meet to institute the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPR: '"Reasonable likelihood" that the petitioner would prevail with respect to at least one challenged claim (intended to be higher than in PGR).'; PGR: '"More likely than not" at least one of the challenged claims is unpatentable.'; Ex Parte Reexamination/Supplemental Examination/Reissue: Raises 'substantial new question' (SNQ) of patentability — i.e., what a reasonable examiner would find important; District Courts: governed by Rules 8, 9, and 11 (pleading standards); ITC: Complainant must plead detailed facts showing unfair act/importation and domestic industry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discovery
rubrics_metrics.description: Scope and availability of discovery in each forum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPR: "Yes, automatic deposition of witnesses submitting declarations or affidavits, automatic discovery of contradictory evidence; additional discovery by motion as necessary in the 'interests of justice'."; PGR: "Yes, automatic deposition of witnesses submitting declarations or affidavits, automatic discovery of contradictory evidence; additional discovery by motion upon showing of 'good cause' and limited to evidence directly related to factual assertion of other party (broader than IPR)."; Ex Parte Reexamination/Reissue/Supplemental Examination: "No (ex parte forums have no discovery)."; District Courts: "Yes, broad and can involve any non‑privileged material that is 'relevant to any party’s claim or defense and proportional to the needs of the case'."; ITC: "Yes, broad, but governed by ITC Rules of Practice and Procedure (19 C.F.R. §§ 210.1 et seq.) and Ground Rules specified by presiding Administrative Law Judge."

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of Proof
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidentiary burden required to prove invalidity or other issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPR/PGR/Ex Parte Reexamination/Reissue/Supplemental Examination: "Preponderance of the evidence."; District Courts/ITC: "'Clear and convincing' evidence (in district court/ITC)."

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim Interpretation Standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim construction standard applied in the forum (e.g., Phillips vs. Broadest Reasonable Interpretation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPR/PGR: "Phillips standard."; Ex Parte Reexamination/Reissue/Supplemental Examination: "Broadest reasonable interpretation."; District Courts/ITC: "Phillips standard."

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for Identification (Real Parties/Disclosure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether real parties in interest must be identified and other disclosure requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPR/PGR: "Must identify all real parties in interest."; Ex Parte Reexamination: "Can be anonymous."; Reissue/Supplemental Examination: "Patent Owner" responsible; District Courts: "Limited to Rule 7.1 disclosure."; ITC: Patent owner or exclusive licensee is the complainant (domestic industry requirement applies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision Maker
rubrics_metrics.description: Who decides the case at the primary forum level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPR/PGR: "Patent Trial and Appeal Board (PTAB) — a panel of 3 Article I Administrative Patent Judges (APJs) who have both law and technical backgrounds."; Ex Parte Reexamination: "Examiner of Central Reexamination Unit."; Reissue/Supplemental Examination: "Examiner."; District Courts: "Article III judge and jury (as applicable)."; ITC: "Administrative Law Judge’s determination reviewed by the Commission."

rubrics_metrics.name: Extent of Estoppel
rubrics_metrics.description: Preclusive effect of an adverse or instituted proceeding on later challenges in other forums.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPR: "The real party in interest and any privy thereto is estopped from challenging the patent in the USPTO, ITC, or district court on any ground the petitioner raised or reasonably could have raised in the IPR."; PGR: "The real party in interest and any privy thereto is estopped from challenging the patent in the USPTO, ITC, or district court on any ground the petitioner raised or reasonably could have been raised in the PGR."; Ex Parte Reexamination/Reissue/Supplemental Examination: "No estoppel applies" (ex parte) or N/A for some; District Courts: "Res judicata and collateral estoppel can apply after final judgment."; ITC: N/A or governed by statute and Commission decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential for Stay of Coordinate Proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Likelihood and conditions under which parallel litigation may be stayed because of the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPR: "Potential stay of litigation depending on many factors."; PGR: "If PGR is filed, then later filed court proceeding automatically stayed."; Ex Parte Reexamination/Reissue/Supplemental Examination: "Stay of litigation possible but unlikely."; District Courts: "N/A (court may grant stays based on circumstances)."; ITC: "Discretionary stay possible (rare)."

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal Forum and Standard of Review
rubrics_metrics.description: Where decisions are appealed and standards applied on review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPR/PGR: "CAFC (both parties); substantial evidence for factfinding and de novo for legal issues."; Ex Parte Reexamination/Reissue/Supplemental Examination: "PTAB, then CAFC (only patentee); substantial evidence for factfinding and de novo for legal issues."; District Courts: "CAFC; substantial evidence for factfinding and de novo for legal issues (for appeals from district court findings)."; ITC: "CAFC; substantial evidence for factfinding and de novo for legal issues."

rubrics_metrics.name: Possibility of Settlement
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether settlement between the parties is possible and any forum limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPR/PGR: "Yes, but PTAB has discretion to continue."; Ex Parte Reexamination: "No (ex parte)."; Reissue/Supplemental Examination: "N/A (procedural limits)."; District Courts: "Yes."; ITC: "Yes."

rubrics_metrics.name: Typical Duration (to Completion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical elapsed time from filing/request to final resolution in the forum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPR: "12–18 months; 6 months if trial phase not instituted."; PGR: "12–18 months; 6 months if trial phase not instituted."; Ex Parte Reexamination: "Approximately 2 years, unless initial request not granted."; Reissue: "Approximately 2–3 years."; Supplemental Examination: "If no SNQ, 3 months; if SNQ, approximately 2–3 years."; District Courts: "Depends on court; approximately 2–5 years."; ITC: "Up to 18 months."

rubrics_metrics.name: Government Fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing and post‑institution governmental fees (as listed) for each proceeding (large entity examples shown).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPR: "$19,000 for up to 20 claims; $375 for each claim thereafter; Post‑institution fee of $22,500 for up to 20 claims; $750 for each claim thereafter."; PGR: "$20,000 for up to 20 claims; $475 for each claim thereafter; Post‑institution fee of $27,500 for up to 20 claims; $1,050 for each claim thereafter."; Ex Parte Reexamination: "$12,600 (large entity, non‑streamlined), $6,300 (large entity, streamlined) for up to 3 independent claims and up to 20 claims total; $480 for each independent claim thereafter, and $100 for each claim in excess of 20 thereafter."; Reissue: "$3,340 (large entity) for up to 3 independent claims and up to 20 claims total; $480 for each independent claim thereafter, and $100 for each claim in excess of 20 thereafter."; Supplemental Examination: "$4,620 (large entity) to file request; $12,700 (large entity) if XPR ordered; $180 for Supplemental Examination Document of 21–50 sheets and $300 for each 50 sheets thereafter."; District Courts: "Depends on court; fees vary."; ITC: "Up to 18 months (fee context in document not specified further)."

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimated Total Average Cost Range
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimated typical total cost ranges (party cost, not just government fees) to resolution in each forum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPR: "$200k–$1.5MM."; PGR: "$200k–$1.5MM."; Ex Parte Reexamination: "$20k–$75k."; Reissue: "$10k–$30k."; Supplemental Examination: "$10k–$30k."; District Courts: "$1.5MM–$6MM."; ITC: "$1.5MM–$6MM."
